data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Ownership allocation systematically suppresses cross-cutting explanations via resource atrophy, measurable by a declining counterfactual success rate of rival lineages over sequential problems.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Rival lineage success rates remain constant or improve over time due to transfer learning.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The owning lineage maintains a perfect success rate, justifying the resource allocation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The first problem in the run already shows 0% rival success, indicating no initial capacity to atrophy.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When problems are assigned exclusively to one lineage, rival lineages are deprived of execution opportunities.
